assumptions.condition: \(M\) is a canonical linear LV-SEM-ME in the sense of Yang et al., Definition 2.
The mixing matrix of \(M\) is identifiable from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) up to permutation and nonzero scaling of its columns.
\(M\) contains the minimum possible number of latent variables among separable canonical LV-SEM-ME representations of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
\(M\) satisfies Yang et al.'s LV-SEM-ME faithfulness rank equalities and strict rank inequalities.

definitions.name: CompletionComplexityDichotomyHandle
definitions.construction: Resolve the exact complexity of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\) by pursuing two auditable branches. For a polynomial branch, eliminate the ordered groups with fraction-free updates while carrying a polynomial-size rank signature, or derive a polynomial separation oracle for the feasible signature set. For a hardness branch, encode coupled downstream zero cancellations by exact rational gadgets and then isolate a nontrivial tractable restriction through dynamic programming on the induced group-interaction graph.

definitions.name: FaithfulPlateauBenchmark
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\) has measured cogent rows \(c_0,c_1,c_2\), measured mleaf rows \(l_0,l_1,l_2\), retained sources \(N_0,N_1,N_2,H_0,H_1\), candidate row pairs \(\{c_i,l_i\}\), candidate source pairs \(\{N_0,H_0\},\{N_1,H_1\},\{N_2\}\), and mixing matrix \[\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0&4&0\\14&1&0&66&16\\168&11&1&782&189\\4&0&0&16&0\\261&18&0&1224&288\\1176&77&7&5479&1323\end{pmatrix}.\]

statements.statement: For every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), the label-restricted recovered candidate sets are pairwise disjoint and \(V=(\bigsqcup_{g=1}^{k}R_g)\sqcup V_{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G,\ell)\). Hence \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)\) is defined uniquely for every \(u\in V\). If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\), then \(u\) is the cogent center in a legal completion exactly when \(r_g=u\), and otherwise it is an mleaf in that group. If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), then \(u\) is a fixed singleton mleaf in every legal completion.
statements.justification: A total label-to-group map is necessary to bind the group index in every intervention-specific image and to separate switchable group members from fixed singleton mleafs.
statements.gap: Yang et al. recover label-restricted AOG groups, but the effect layer requires the induced per-label partition and fixed-mleaf branch to be stated explicitly.
statements.consumer: The partition makes every subsequent intervention-specific effect set a well-defined function of its displayed arguments.

statements.statement: For every \(\omega\in\Omega(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), all pivots in \(\Delta_{\omega}\) are nonzero, \(Q_{\omega}\) is unit lower triangular in group order, and \(M_{\omega}\) obtained from \(A_{\omega},B^{C}_{\omega},D_{\omega},B^{L}_{\omega}\) is a legal canonical reconstruction whose retained mixing matrix is exactly \(W\). The construction is invariant to independent nonzero rescaling of the columns of \(W\).
statements.justification: Choice-specific pivot normalization is required before any mixing-column ratio can represent a labeled intervention effect.
statements.gap: Yang et al.'s Algorithm 2 reconstructs from a chosen row and column assignment, but its displayed formulas do not isolate the column-rescaling invariant normalization used by the proposed effect image.
statements.consumer: Every subsequent image value and countermodel is computed from this legal normalized reconstruction.

For every legal choice \(\omega\in\Omega(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\) and \(u,v\in V\), \[	au_{\omega}(v\leftarrow u)= egin{cases}1,&v=u,\0,&v
e u	ext{ and }g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)= ot,\0,&v

e u,\W_{v c_g}/W_{u c_g},&g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]	ext{ and }\omega_g=(u,c_g).\end{cases}\] Thus, on the cogent-group branch, changing choices outside the uniquely bound group \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)\) leaves the entire \(u\)-intervention column unchanged; on the fixed singleton-mleaf branch every off-diagonal effect is zero.
statements.justification: This locality identity converts an exponentially large model class into a projection of feasible local choices.
statements.gap: Tramontano et al. analyze column swaps without simultaneous measurement-label and center reassignment; Yang et al. do not state the all-pairs total-effect projection.
statements.consumer: The identity lets an analyst report all possible effects of one labeled exposure without reconstructing unrelated DOG coordinates.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), and every \(u,v\in V\), the complete image of \(\tau_{\omega}(v\leftarrow u)\) over all minimum-edge DOG representatives is exactly \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) in \(\text{def:effect-image}\), and \(|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|\leq q+1\). For every \(s\in S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) there is an attaining \(\omega_s\in\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\); if the image is not a singleton, two such minimum completions furnish observationally equivalent countermodels with unequal labeled total effects. The qualifier is relative Zariski generic over each real canonical coefficient variety, equivalently Lebesgue-almost-everywhere in each stratum's free coefficient coordinates, while source-law separability remains a separate assumption; no probability claim is made for rational inputs.
statements.justification: The exact set, not a selected representative, is the population object required for honest causal reporting under DOG equivalence.
statements.gap: Salehkaleybar et al. project latent-variable LiNGAM ambiguity onto effects, but their admissible transformations omit measured-variable center changes and known measurement labels; Yang et al. give only a four-node robustness example.
statements.consumer: A measurement-error analyst can distinguish a robust effect from a finite list of observationally indistinguishable alternatives and receive attaining models for sensitivity analysis.

For every population tuple covered by \(	ext{thm:complete-effect-image}\) and every \(u,v\in V\), singletonness follows by direct equality comparison in the displayed image. Precisely, \( |S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|=1\) if and only if one of the following mutually compatible branches holds: \(v=u\); \(v

The common value is one when \(v=u\), zero on the fixed singleton-mleaf branch and on either cogent-group branch admitting zero, and \(W_{vc}/W_{uc}\) for any admissible \(c\in L_u(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\) in the remaining branch.
statements.justification: This transparent algebraic corollary tells a consumer how to read singletonness and its common value directly from the exact image.
statements.gap: The contribution is the complete mixed-DOG image; the zero and cross-multiplication conditions are its direct finite-set equality test and are not advertised as an independently defined certification theorem.
statements.consumer: An analyst can test whether the reported finite image collapses without introducing a second diagnostic object whose definition merely restates singletonness.

statements.statement: The instance \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\) is canonical, minimal, and LV-SEM-ME rank-faithful. Among its thirty-two legal reconstructions, \(e^{\star}=12\), and exactly four completions attain the optimum: each selects \(N_i\) as the structural noise, selects \(c_2\) as the third center, and independently selects \(c_i\) or \(l_i\) as the first two centers. The choice \(((c_0,N_0),(c_1,H_1),(l_2,N_2))\) has thirteen edges, every one-group change has at least thirteen edges, and a simultaneous repair of the second noise and third center attains twelve.
statements.justification: The faithful plateau rules out strict coordinate descent and any additive per-group edge score before they can contaminate the main algorithm.
statements.gap: Neither Yang et al.'s Cartesian enumeration nor adjacent equivalence-class enumeration papers isolate a faithful coupled-cancellation benchmark of this form.
statements.consumer: Any proposed polynomial completion solver must recover this exact optimum and four-model plateau as its first destructive unit test.

statements.statement: Determine the exact computational complexity of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\) for exactly encoded rational \(\widetilde W\in\mathbb Q^{p\times q}\) satisfying the canonical-model promise, both without a prescribed pair and with one prescribed local pair. Resolve one of two branches: either construct a deterministic algorithm \(\mathsf A_{\min}\) that returns an attaining legal completion or an infeasibility certificate in time polynomial in \(p\), \(q\), and the input bit length, or prove an exact hardness classification and identify a nontrivial structurally restricted tractable regime. The resolution must use the elimination, separation-oracle, or rational cancellation-gadget handle in \(\text{def:completion-handle}\), account for coupled downstream cancellations, and correctly recover the optimum and complete minimizer projection of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\).
statements.justification: A genuine algorithm-versus-hardness classification is the unresolved step governing whether the exact population image can be computed scalably on the full published class.
statements.gap: Yang et al.'s Algorithm 2 has a multiplicative Cartesian choice factor, but enumeration cost proves neither polynomial solvability nor hardness; maximum-flow identification and linear-delay MEC traversal solve different combinatorial objects.
statements.consumer: The classification will either supply a scalable exact image routine or delimit the structural regimes in which exact mixed-DOG effect reporting is computationally feasible.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf A_{\min}\) solves every rational instance of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\) in polynomial bit time, then one unconstrained call computes \(e^{\star}\), and at most \(\sum_{g=1}^{k}|R_g||K_g|\leq pq\) constrained calls compute every \(P_g(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell)\) and one attaining minimum completion for each retained pair. The resulting exact algorithm computes every \(S_{vu}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), its common value when it is a singleton, and two attaining countermodels whenever it is not, using \(O(p^2q)\) additional rational operations; singletonness is checked directly by the zero and cross-multiplication comparisons in \(\text{prop:singleton-minor-corollary}\).
statements.justification: The reduction separates the unresolved global optimization from polynomial image projection, equality checking, and witness extraction.
statements.gap: IDA and lvLiNGAM certification exploit local graphical choices, whereas the mixed DOG projection requires global minimum-feasibility queries before local values can be trusted.
statements.consumer: The reduction gives an implementation contract and prevents an effect-image routine from combining locally possible choices that never coexist in a minimum model.

statements.statement: On the real subclass with no measured substantive variables and no mleaf rows, and for \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) reduces to the normalized mixing-column effect set of latent-variable LiNGAM. On this shared generic subclass, \(|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|=1\) if and only if the total effect of \(u\) on \(v\) satisfies Tramontano et al.'s unknown-graph criterion in Theorem 3.3.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that the mixed-model image agrees with the complete published criterion when measurement error disappears.
statements.gap: The proposition claims equivalence only on the shared no-measurement generic subclass and does not relabel the published lvLiNGAM theorem as new.
statements.consumer: Existing lvLiNGAM users obtain a backward-compatible effect image while gaining the mixed-model extension when noisy measurements are introduced.

sampling_model.design: Population exact identification on the real generic domain of Yang et al.'s recovered mixing equivalence class, with exact rational encoding used only for the separate completion-complexity question.
sampling_model.units: The population layer is indexed by the observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). An optional region-union remark may start from \(n\) i.i.d. observations, but no first-stage inferential construction is a contribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes a labeled substantive variable \(u\), including a variable measured with error or a fixed singleton mleaf.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used because the population target is a linear structural intervention effect recovered from the mixing representation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population core takes real \(W\) as the separable identification input. Rational \(\widetilde W\) is introduced only for exact \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) bit complexity. Construction, alignment, and computation of any confidence region for an overcomplete mixing matrix are outside scope.

estimand_functional: \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)=\{1\}\) for \(v=u\); for \(v\ne u\) and \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), it equals \(\{0\}\); on the cogent-group branch it equals \(\{W_{vc}/W_{uc}:c\in L_u(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\}\cup(\{0\}\text{ if }z_u(W,\mathcal G,\ell)=1)\), with singletonness read directly from equality of these displayed values.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithm 2 enumerates all row and column choices and then retains the models with the fewest structural edges.
Theorem 3.3 gives a necessary-and-sufficient generic criterion for an observed-variable total effect when the causal graph is unknown.
Section 4 computes the observationally compatible causal-effect possibilities in latent-variable LiNGAM and gives conditions for uniqueness.
Theorem 4.3 certifies generic coefficient identification under general confounding by polynomially many maximum-flow computations.
The paper enumerates Markov-equivalent DAGs with linear delay and bounded structural change between consecutive outputs.
IDA computes possible intervention effects from local CPDAG information without enumerating every DAG in the equivalence class.

tldr: Yang et al. identify a real canonical linear model with simultaneous latent confounding and measurement error only generically up to a minimum-edge DOG class, and their recovery algorithm enumerates a Cartesian product of center and noise assignments. The project proves that the known observation labels induce a unique total map from every intervention label to either one cogent AOG group or a fixed singleton-mleaf branch. Its headline theorem gives every labeled pairwise total-effect image exactly as normalized entries from that intervention variable's globally feasible source columns, augmented by zero when the variable can be an mleaf, and supplies an attaining minimum model for every value. Singletonness is a transparent corollary obtained by zero checks and cross-multiplication among all admissible source columns, not an independent certificate target. The central open object is a genuine complexity dichotomy for exact rational globally constrained minimum completion under coupled downstream cancellations: either a polynomial algorithm or an exact hardness result with a nontrivial tractable restriction.

project_justification.gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 identifies the real mixed model generically only up to DOG equivalence, Section 5 treats one four-node effect, and Algorithm 2 uses an exponential Cartesian loop. Salehkaleybar et al. and Tramontano et al. characterize effect ambiguity without simultaneous measurement error. No located result projects every labeled mixed-model effect through globally minimum center and noise choices or classifies the complexity of coupled rational minimum completion.
project_justification.niche: Total effects have a choice-local normalized-column representation once the observation-group map and fixed singleton-mleaf branch are explicit, even though minimum-edge feasibility of a local choice is globally coupled. This separation permits an exact algebraic image theorem over the real generic domain and concentrates computational uncertainty in one auditable exact optimization problem.
project_justification.fill: The project delivers the complete \(q+1\)-point effect image with attaining countermodels, records its singleton equality test as a direct corollary, proves a faithful plateau obstruction to greedy optimization, poses an algorithm-versus-hardness classification for rational constrained minimum completion, gives the corresponding polynomial projection reduction, and verifies the no-measurement reduction.

related_work: Yang, Nafea, Kiyavash, Zhang, and Ghassami (2026), Definition 2, Theorems 2--3, Algorithm 2, Proposition 6, Appendix A.2, and Appendix A.4 define the real canonical model, its label-restricted AOG recovery, and the generic DOG equivalence class used here. Their generic qualification is interpreted stratumwise: the excluded proper algebraic loci have Lebesgue measure zero in the free coefficient coordinates of each nonempty real canonical coefficient stratum, with separability imposed separately on the source laws. Their algorithm enumerates every center and noise selection, with complexity proportional to \(M_{\mathrm{Row}}M_{\mathrm{Col}}\), and Section 5 analyzes robustness only in a four-node union model. Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020), Section 4, provide the closest effect-image precedent by enumerating compatible latent-variable LiNGAM parameterizations; measurement-label restrictions and mleaf center changes are absent. Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (2024), Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, and 3.11, turn admissible mixing-column swaps into complete generic total-effect criteria and a cubic-time graphical procedure when measurement error is absent. Proposition \(\text{prop:no-measurement-reduction}\) promises equivalence on that shared real generic subclass rather than a strict improvement. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026), Theorems 3.6, 4.2, and 4.3, convert determinant ranks and nonintersecting paths into maximum-flow identification tests under a different general-confounding model; this informs a possible positive branch of the complexity question but does not optimize mixed DOG completions. Wienoebst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liskiewicz (2023) obtain linear-delay traversal of a Markov equivalence class, which informs local update control but not a global algebraic sparsity optimum. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009) compute possible DAG effects from local CPDAG information; the mixed-DOG minimum-feasibility projection is not locally rectangular. Romano and Shaikh (2010) supply general identified-set honesty terminology for the optional external premise, not a construction of an aligned overcomplete-ICA region or a contribution of this core.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact effect image requires only the projected globally minimum pairs \(P_g(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), but computing those pairs is not known to factor across groups. The faithful benchmark has a strict coordinate-descent trap at thirteen edges and a coupled repair reaching the twelve-edge global optimum, so scalar per-group costs, strict greedy descent, and unqualified local-switch connectivity are invalid routes. Population identification is stated for real parameters on Yang et al.'s stratumwise generic domain; rational exact input \(\widetilde W\) is used only for \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) bit complexity, with no probability assertion on \(\mathbb Q^{p\times q}\).
honest_scope: The core fixes Yang et al.'s real canonical, separable, minimal, LV-SEM-ME rank-faithful class with known observation labels. Equality between the recovered minimum DOG and the full observational equivalence class is asserted only for \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), a relative Zariski-open set on each nonempty real canonical coefficient variety whose complement is Lebesgue-null in the stratum's free coefficient coordinates; separability is a separate source-law assumption. The finite projected image is exact once \(W\), \(\mathcal G(W,\ell)\), and \(\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) are fixed. The observation-group partition, normalized reconstruction, local effect column, exact projected image, its direct singleton equality corollary, plateau certificate, conditional oracle reduction, and no-measurement reduction are theorem obligations. The exact complexity of constrained minimum completion on rational inputs is the first-class unresolved question: a valid resolution may be polynomial solvability or an exact hardness theorem coupled with a nontrivial tractable restriction. When there are no measured variables or mleaf rows, the image criterion must collapse generically to Tramontano et al.'s Theorem 3.3. Self-effects equal one, and a fixed singleton-mleaf intervention has zero off-diagonal effects. Inference construction is outside scope. As an unnumbered definitional remark only, \(\text{ass:first-stage-coverage}\) and \(W\in\mathcal C_n\) imply \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\subseteq\mathcal E_n(v,u)\) simultaneously for every \(u,v\in V\), so the same event has probability at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\). This is set inclusion from the definition of the union; the core neither constructs the aligned region nor counts the transfer as a theorem or contribution.

literature_map: The direct anchor is Yang et al. (2026). Definition 2 fixes the real canonical mixed model, Assumptions 1, 3, and 4 supply separability, rank faithfulness, and minimality, Theorems 2--3 identify the model generically up to the DOG class, Algorithm 2 enumerates center and noise choices, Proposition 6 identifies DOG members by global minimum edge count, Appendix A.2 gives the simultaneous switch construction, and Appendix A.4 gives the generic DOG argument. The effect-image thread is Salehkaleybar et al. (2020), Section 4, and Tramontano et al. (2024), Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, and 3.11. Those results show that projecting observational ambiguity onto total effects can yield complete criteria, but their transformations have neither measurement labels nor a fixed singleton-mleaf branch. The algorithmic thread is Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026), Theorems 3.6 and 4.2--4.3, where determinant ranks become nonintersecting-path maxima and maximum flow, and Wienoebst et al. (2023), where local equivalence moves support linear-delay MEC enumeration. Neither thread classifies Yang et al.'s rational edge-count reconstruction under cancellations across multiple groups. Maathuis et al. (2009) provide a local projection precedent for a different, rectangular graphical ambiguity structure.

novelty_justification: The closest population comparator is Tramontano et al. (2024): Theorems 3.3 and 3.8 give complete generic total-effect criteria in lvLiNGAM, and Theorem 3.11 gives a cubic graphical procedure. The proposal does not claim the normalized mixing-column idea as new and must reproduce their unknown-graph criterion on the shared real generic no-measurement subclass. The strict delta is the complete image for the mixed DOG transformation: known observation labels map each intervention label to either one cogent candidate group or a fixed singleton-mleaf branch; within a cogent group the label may switch between center and mleaf, pivot normalization changes jointly with the selected structural noise, and only pairs attained inside a globally minimum reconstruction enter the image. The zero and minor comparisons for singletonness are presented only as transparent algebraic consequences of that image. Yang et al. (2026) provide the real mixed equivalence class on a stratumwise generic domain but enumerate every joint assignment and analyze one four-node effect. The computational kernel asks for the exact algorithm-versus-hardness classification of rational minimum completion; the faithful plateau establishes nonadditivity but does not prejudge either branch. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026) and Wienoebst et al. (2023) inform possible positive techniques without subsuming the coupled completion problem. No inferential construction or coverage-transfer identity is counted toward novelty.
